evidence: smtps-465-relays-the-client-login-to-the-backend: baseline 67-81 declare the SMTPS mailhost on $smtps_port with ssl, smtp_auth 'login plain' and raw_prepend 'proxy_smtp_auth on;'; the probe logs in over TLS on 127.0.0.1:465 and expects AUTH 235 then RCPT/DATA accepted by a backend whose 465 service accepts a recipient only from a SASL-authenticated sender (permit_sasl_authenticated, reject), so the queued message is only possible if nginx passed the login on, as proxy_smtp_auth on states; the effect is the server's protocol replies (backend acceptance), cross-checked on the peer by the-backend-received-the-sessions-from-the-proxy

smtp-25-delivers-through-the-proxy: baseline 116-124 declare smtp_auth_stream proxying to ${mail_backend}:${smtp_port} on 9925 with proxy_ssl off (reached via the 4244 auth server's Auth-Port 9925, lines 150-160, and the port-25 mailhost with smtp_auth none / proxy_smtp_auth off, 83-94); the probe sends an unauthenticated message to 127.0.0.1:25 and expects the backend's 250 'queued as', which can only come through that plaintext stream to the backend's port 25; supported

nginx-config-valid-and-running: baseline 54 opens the imaps mailhost, one of the nginx mail/stream/server resources the class declares; nginx -t succeeding and the service active is the direct precondition of that configuration taking effect under the params fixture, and it fails on the clean node (no nginx); supported, if broad
